rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes only a comment string from '// Load 4 elements at once' to '// Load 5 elements at once' on line 18 of the CUDA source. Comments in C/C++ are stripped during compilation and produce no machine code. The actual executable code (loading in_vec.x through in_vec.w, computing sigmoid for 4 elements, storing as float4) remains completely unchanged.
rounds.survival_reason: This mutation is a pure comment change in the CUDA source code. The mutation tool's 'const_perturb' operator targeted the integer '4' inside the comment string '// Load 4 elements at once' rather than an actual numeric constant in executable code. In C/C++, comments are ignored by the compiler and have zero effect on the generated binary. The actual kernel logic - idx calculation, the idx+3<size boundary check, float4 load/store operations, and sigmoid computation - all remain identical. Layer 2 testing confirmed bitwise equivalence across 112 test rounds, which is the expected outcome when only a comment differs.
rounds.kill_strategy: unkillable - the mutation only modifies a comment string in the CUDA kernel source code, which has absolutely no effect on compilation or runtime behavior. No possible input values can distinguish between the original and mutated kernels because they compile to identical machine code.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing tools should implement comment detection to exclude numeric literals that appear within comment strings (// or /* */) from the mutation target pool. This prevents generation of trivially equivalent mutants that waste testing resources and pollute mutation scores.
